from.place: Proof (1): 'followed by $R\Gamma_c(X,\nu_n)$, gives $P_{n+1}\otimes^L A_n\cong R\Gamma_c(X,K_{n+1}\otimes^LA_n)\cong P_n$; for the stalks, ... gives $P_{\bar y,n+1}\otimes^LA_n\cong(K_{n+1}\otimes^LA_n)_{\bar y}\cong P_{\bar y,n}$': the passage from the sheaf-level reduction isomorphism to the reduction of the coefficient complex, i.e. evaluation at the algebraically closed point commuting with finite reduction, used there without statement.

title: Sections at an algebraically closed point commute with finite coefficient reduction
statement:
Let $\kappa$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $t=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with its small pro-etale site $t_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\Gamma(t,-)$ be the sections over the final object $\operatorname{id}_t$, on derived categories [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $\kappa$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_i=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^i$ for $i\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $(A_i)_t$ for the constant sheaf of rings on $t_{\mathrm{proet}}$, so that $\Gamma(t,(A_i)_t)=A_i$, and $D(t_{\mathrm{proet}},A_i)$, $D(A_i)$ for the derived categories of $(A_i)_t$-modules and of $A_i$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $n\geq j\geq1$ and let $N\in D(t_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ have cohomology sheaves vanishing outside a finite interval of degrees. Let $N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j\in D(t_{\mathrm{proet}},A_j)$ be the derived change of rings along $(A_n)_t\to(A_j)_t$, and $\Gamma(t,N)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j\in D(A_j)$ the derived change of rings along $A_n\to A_j$, both as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then there is an isomorphism
$$
\Gamma(t,N)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Gamma\bigl(t,N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j\bigr)
$$
in $D(A_j)$, natural in $N$, equal to the identity for $j=n$, and compatible with successive reductions: for $n\geq j\geq i\geq1$ the isomorphism for $(n,i)$ is the composite of the isomorphism for $(n,j)$ reduced to $A_i$ and the isomorphism for $(j,i)$ applied to $N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j$, under the associativity identifications $(-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_j}A_i\cong-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_i$.
